overview: Timer is a four-line world-category scaler that writes its Speed value (0.1 to 10, default 2) into mc.timer.timerSpeed on every UpdateEvent. The vanilla Timer accumulator consumes wall-clock milliseconds scaled by the speed value, so the effective game-tick rate scales linearly with the setting: the default 2 runs the client at roughly 40 ticks per second, doubling the emission rate of every serverbound stream the tick drives. onDisable restores the field to 1F, and a WorldEvent handler turns the module off whenever the client leaves a world, so the scalar cannot survive a respawn or a server transfer. The module constructs no packets; its fingerprint is entirely the accelerated ledger traffic, which is why the countering set lives in the C00 and C0F corpora.

sections.p: The module is three handlers: onUpdate writes mc.timer.timerSpeed = speedValue.get() on every fired UpdateEvent, onDisable restores 1F when the player exists, and onWorld sets state = false when the incoming WorldEvent carries a null worldClient. UpdateEvent (Events.kt line 204) fires once per game tick, so the write is continuous, not a one-shot latch: the field is re-asserted every tick the module stays on. The Speed setting spans 0.1 to 10 with a default of 2, so the out-of-box behavior is a doubled client.

No packet object is constructed anywhere in the file; the scalar acts on the tick clock that drives the whole client. The vanilla Timer contract, described from stock 1.8 because the snapshot ships no net/minecraft tree, is a partial-tick accumulator scaled by timerSpeed, so the effective tick rate equals 20 times the setting: the default 2 produces about 40 C03 movement packets per second plus the accelerated C00 keepalive echoes and C0F transaction confirmations. MixinMinecraft in this client shadows fields such as rightClickDelayTimer but adds no timerSpeed hook, so the module's write reaches the vanilla field directly.

Windowed rate checks tolerate the transient spikes of a pulse timer but the sustained scalar is a steady doubling, which pushes the movement rate window permanently positive. Inter-delay checks measure the spacing between consecutive packets against the 50ms tick expectation and fail within a few packets of the speed-up. The module is symmetric while the checks are not: sub-1 settings (0.1 to 0.9) slow the client and pass the one-directional clock checks by design, and the onDisable restore is the only guard against a stuck field on toggle-off.

files.label: Timer.kt
files.explanation: The entire module: the timerSpeed write in onUpdate, the onDisable restore, and the world-unload disable. The brief pins C00 and C0F, which the module never constructs: those streams are the keepalive echoes and transaction confirmations that the accelerated tick clock emits at double rate, and the countering checks measure them.

files.label: Events.kt (UpdateEvent tick hook)
files.explanation: UpdateEvent (line 204) is the per-tick carrier the module hooks to re-assert timerSpeed; it is the only verifiable wiring between the module and the tick clock because the snapshot ships no net/minecraft tree, so the vanilla Timer accumulator that consumes the value has to be described from the stock contract.

countering.label: MorePackets (movement rate window)
countering.explanation: MorePackets scores every processed move into an ActionFrequency with 500ms buckets against a 22 packet/s ceiling with 20 ideal, plus a half-second burst path (15 direct, 10 direct-violation). The default 2x setting sustains about 40 C03/s, so the window accumulator runs permanently positive and cancels at vl > 2 with a set-back seeded from SurvivalFly; settings below about 1.1 stay under the effective floor because idle windows burn the excess.

countering.label: KeepAliveFrequency (keepalive ledger)
countering.explanation: The ledger tracks S00 ids against C00 echoes and counts replies that arrive late, duplicated or with no pending request. The accelerated loop can drain a batched keepalive delivery into a single second-bucket, which is the one case that trips it; a steady 2x passes the ledger because the echo cadence stays tied to the server's S00 rate. Its structural role here is the gate: Frequency TimerA refuses to run without a recently accepted keepalive, so this check arms the timer layer.

countering.label: TimerA (inter-delay deviation)
countering.explanation: TimerA measures the delay between consecutive C03s against the 50ms tick expectation through MovingStats(20) with a stddev gate of 7.07, accumulating allowance += 50 - delay and failing when the balance passes the floor. At 2x the delays collapse to about 25ms, so the check fails within two packets of the speed-up; sub-1 settings drain the allowance and pass by design, and the check is gated on a recently accepted keepalive and exempt ticks.

countering.label: Timer (transaction-anchored balance)
countering.explanation: Grim runs a 50ms balance per movement packet against a real-time clock whose baseline is anchored to the C0F stream: knownPlayerClockTime is refreshed only after a movement followed by a PONG or WINDOW_CONFIRMATION. The default clockDrift of 120ms is consumed within a few ticks at 2x, so the doubled C03 rate flags promptly; the check is one-directional, so sub-1 settings pass because limitFallBehind absorbs the slow phase, which matches the module's symmetric scalar against asymmetric checks.
